level1.text: Two pulses travel towards each other on a string. Both displace the string upwards, one by at most $2.5\,\text{cm}$ and the other by $1.5\,\text{cm}$. How large is the greatest displacement of the string at the moment when the peaks of the pulses are on top of each other?

Two pulses meet on a string. One displaces the string by at most $3.0\,\text{cm}$ upwards, the other by $1.2\,\text{cm}$ downwards. What is the displacement of the string at the point where the centres of the pulses are on top of each other? Upwards is the positive direction. Give the answer with its sign in centimetres.

Two loudspeakers in phase play a sound with a wavelength of $0.60\,\text{m}$. At four listening points the path difference is a) $0.60\,\text{m}$, b) $0.90\,\text{m}$, c) $1.20\,\text{m}$ and d) $1.50\,\text{m}$. Is the interference at each point constructive or destructive? Justify.
level1.answer: a) constructive; b) destructive; c) constructive; d) destructive

level1.text: Two loudspeakers in phase play a sound with a wavelength of $0.68\,\text{m}$. What is the smallest path difference at which the sound is weak at the listening point? Give the answer in metres.

Two sources in a ripple tank vibrate in phase, and the wavelength is $1.5\,\text{cm}$. On the perpendicular bisector there is the line of constructive interference $n = 0$, and on each side of it the next ones are $n = 1$ and $n = 2$. How large is the path difference on the line $n = 2$? Give the answer in centimetres.

level2.text: Two loudspeakers A and B in phase are $1.20\,\text{m}$ apart. A listener stands $1.60\,\text{m}$ from loudspeaker B directly in front of it, so that the line between the listener and loudspeaker B is perpendicular to the line between the loudspeakers. What is the greatest wavelength at which it is quiet at the listener's position? Give the answer in metres.

Two sources in a ripple tank vibrate in phase at a frequency of $15\,\text{Hz}$, and the waves travel at a speed of $0.30\,\text{m/s}$. Point Q is on the nodal line nearest to the perpendicular bisector, and it is $9.0\,\text{cm}$ from source $S_2$, which is the nearer one. How far is point Q from source $S_1$? Give the answer in centimetres.

Two sources in a ripple tank vibrate in phase, and the wavelength is $2.0\,\text{cm}$. The path from source $S_1$ to point R is $14.0\,\text{cm}$ and from source $S_2$ $9.0\,\text{cm}$. Source $S_1$ vibrates more strongly: the amplitude of its wave at point R is $3.0\,\text{mm}$ and that of the wave from $S_2$ is $2.0\,\text{mm}$. What is the amplitude of the vibration of the water at point R? Give the answer in millimetres.

Two equally large pulses of the same shape travel towards each other on a long taut string, one above the string and the other below it. The distance between the centres of the pulses is at first $1.20\,\text{m}$, and each pulse travels at a speed of $0.40\,\text{m/s}$. How long does it take before the string is completely straight for a moment? Give the answer in seconds.

level3.text: On a sports field two loudspeakers in phase are $3.0\,\text{m}$ apart, and they play a sound with a frequency of $340\,\text{Hz}$. The speed of sound is $340\,\text{m/s}$. A listener walks along a long straight path that runs in front of the loudspeakers parallel to the line between them, from far to the left to far to the right. How many quiet spots does the listener pass? Justify why there are only a finite number of quiet spots. Assume that the sound is not reflected from anywhere.

The frequency of two sources in phase in a ripple tank can be adjusted, and the speed of the wave in the tank is $24\,\text{cm/s}$. A point T is marked in the tank. When the frequency is $10\,\text{Hz}$, the water at point T stays at rest. When the frequency is raised, the water at point T is next at rest at the frequency $14\,\text{Hz}$. How large is the path difference at point T? Give the answer in centimetres.

A harbour breakwater has two narrow gaps, $16.0\,\text{m}$ apart. At sea the waves come straight towards the breakwater, so that the wave crests are parallel to it. The waves coming through the gaps spread into the harbour. A boat is anchored $30.0\,\text{m}$ from one gap, directly in front of it perpendicular to the breakwater, and the boat is on the nodal line nearest to the perpendicular bisector of the gaps, where the water is almost calm. Justify why the gaps act like two sources in phase, and calculate the wavelength of the waves. Give the answer in metres.
